sentences.text: Petitioners have filed this writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India making a prayer to issue writ of mandamus commanding respondent nos. 2 and 3 to decide objection submitted by them against compensation awarded to them vide order dated 6.7.2021.

2. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondents submitted that land of petitioners has not been acquired and compensation has not been given for acquisition of their land under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'Act of 2013').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Mining Rights were given to respondents as per provision of Section 247(4)
of the M.P. Land Revenue Code, 1959.
Since respondents by doing mining will disturb or infringe upon the rights of owner of land, therefore, compensation is to be granted to owner.

Compensation is calculated as per the principles laid down under the Act of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:50651 2 WP-25232-2021 2013 but order is passed under Land Revenue Code,
therefore, petitioners may prefer an appeal against the order of compensation if they are aggrieved by the same.
It is also submitted that compensation amount has already been deposited by the respondents.
No interference is called for in the petition and same may be dismissed.
3. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: 4. On going through the facts of the case, it is found that compensation has been awarded to petitioners by order of SDO dated 17.1.2019.
Award is passed under the provision of M.P. Land Revenue Code adopting the principles of the Act of 2013 for quantifying the compensation amount.
Petitioners are having remedy to prefer an appeal against the order passed by Sub Divisional Officer.

Since petitioners are having remedy to prefer an appeal, therefore, they may challenge the quantum of compensation by preferring an appeal before the Appellate Authority as per provision of Section 44 of the M.P. Land Revenue Code, 1959.
5.
With the aforesaid, petition is disposed off.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE AD/
